en.pageTitle: FreeSpeech SAAC: accessible augmentative communicator - Diego Mena
en.cardTitle: FreeSpeech SAAC: augmentative communicator in Vue 3 with WCAG 2.2 AA
en.cardDesc: Augmentative and Alternative Communication (AAC) system in Vue 3.5 + Vite with WCAG 2.2 AA conformance, 345 offline ARASAAC pictograms and a universal SDK adaptable for LMS and web portals.

articles.article11-p1: People with communication disabilities rely on augmentative and alternative communication systems (AAC) to express themselves, but most commercial options are expensive or require installed apps. FreeSpeech SAAC is a pictogram communicator that runs in the browser, built with Vue 3.5 + Vite and designed with WCAG 2.2 AA conformance from the ground up.
articles.article11-p2: The visual vocabulary uses the ARASAAC catalog, the open reference in pictography for augmentative communication. The 345 pictograms are served locally, so the communicator works offline: a critical requirement in classrooms, rural areas or institutions with restricted networks.
articles.article11-h2-2: Accessibility that is practiced, not just preached
articles.article11-p3: Being a tool for people with disabilities demanded an exemplary standard: touch targets of at least 24x24 px (2.5.8), AA contrast in all states, full keyboard navigation, live regions for the constructed phrase and voice synthesis via the Web Speech API to vocalize each selection.
articles.article11-p4: Beyond the full application at freespeech.a11ypro.tech, the project includes an SDK integrable into LMS platforms and web portals. The host can configure the trigger (button, keyboard shortcut or custom element) without touching the communicator's core.
articles.article11-p5: Communicating is a right. A web-based, free, offline and accessible AAC removes the economic and technical barriers that leave many people without an alternative voice today. Publishing it as open source aims to let any institution deploy and adapt it without licenses.
articles.article11-p6: The project is open source at github.com/ingelectronicadj/freespeech.
